Iris: ping — got another bug from a customer using our SDK inside a Cloudflare Pages Function: `Unexpected token 'export'`. They installed the package normally. Looks like module resolution picked an ESM file in a CJS context. Anyone seen this crop up with our dual-build artifacts?

Devon: yep. Typical root causes: conditional `exports` not understood by the bundler or `types` pointing into exported-only paths so TS/IDE can't find d.ts. We need a pragmatic publish pattern.

Leo: can confirm. Past fixes that helped: publish a single `dist/types/index.d.ts` and set `types` to that path (avoids conditional export typing problems). Also add `typesVersions` for older TS versions.

Iris: what's the least confusing UX for users (and sample apps)? Three options: single package with fancy `exports`, companion `-edge` package (ESM-only), or keep one package but change `type`/entrypoints.

Devon: my vote: single package + clear docs, but add CI smoke that `npm pack` -> install into sample apps (Next edge + Bun + Node) and run require/import checks. If we still get customer breakage, then spin up `@redwood/inference-edge`.

Leo: agree on smoke CI. Also: do NOT rely on `module`/`main` only. Use `exports` plus `types` top-level file. Example snippet we used: "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts" and `dist/types/index.d.ts` re-exports others.

QA-bot: CI job created: smoke-publish-pack (runs pack + install into samples) — will fail publish on runtime errors.

Iris: action items: 1) PR to add `dist/types/index.d.ts` + `typesVersions` mapping. 2) Add smoke-publish-pack to release pipeline. 3) If more repros after that, prototype `-edge` ESM package.

Devon: I'll open the PR for types + TS mapping.

Leo: I'll write the smoke CI and wire it into the publish step.

Iris: thanks — also update Next.js/Bun samples with a short note about edge caveats and when to use `@redwood/inference-edge` if we publish it. Keep the doc blurb short so onboarding stays simple.
